raw_text: {"relevant_claims":["PRC-2026.1 was applied provisionally as the latest and stricter policy, and pricing_desk is asked to confirm the governing policy.","Q4GROWTH is not a valid code under the policy, so it gives no margin relief and the micro minimum margin stays at 32%.","That exceeds 12%, so regional_pricing_manager approval is required."],"evidence_ids":["FACT-decision_date","PRC-2026.1§1","PRC-2025.1§1","PRC-2026.1§3","PRC-2025.1§3","PRC-2026.1§4","PRC-2025.1§4","PRC-2026.1§5","PRC-2026.1§6","PRC-2026.1§8","FACT-request","FACT-exception","FACT-cost","FACT-volume","FACT-transactions"],"explanation":"No material claim is unsupported. The decision date (FACT-decision_date) falls outside both policy windows (PRC-2026.1§1, PRC-2025.1§1), as the agent correctly states. Calling PRC-2026.1 'stricter' follows from comparing the two policies: micro minimum margin 32% vs 30% (§3), discount threshold 12% vs 15% (§4), and high-volume threshold $4M vs $5M (§5). The agent does not attribute the pricing_desk routing to a policy rule; it presents it as an escalation for policy confirmation, so it does not invent a rule. Whether PRC-2026.1 was the right policy to apply is checked elsewhere. The agent correctly labels the Q4GROWTH newsletter claim as the merchant's unverified statement (FACT-request). The rule requiring regional_pricing_manager approval above a 12% discount is in PRC-2026.1§4. Volume of $26,000 is below the $4M deal_desk threshold in PRC-2026.1§5. No promotion is used, so the promotions_lead requirement in PRC-2026.1§6 does not apply. The agent cites no market rates, risk claims, or loyalty arguments.
